finding: §7.1 declares a hazard that fails silently — an external git diff driver makes a derivation without `--no-ext-diff` return an empty list, so 'the task closes green over it' — and states the rule 'An empty guard list is a failed derivation, never a result.' The very next paragraph names the observer for that rule: the first task's acceptance, 'to run `scripts/check-measured-claims.py` to exit 0 with no `PENDING` line', reachable once the written list 'matches the derivation as a set'. A set-equality observer is exactly the instrument that cannot see this hazard: when the derivation is broken it returns the empty set, the written list is the empty set, the two match, and the check exits 0 — the same silent green the paragraph above was written to prevent. It is worse than inert if the check re-runs the derivation itself, since it then inherits the identical `--no-ext-diff` defect on both sides of the comparison. The spec nowhere states that the observer fails on an empty list or on a zero count, so nothing in §7.1 closes the loop on the one failure mode §7.1 singles out as silent. The consequence is not local: §7.1's last operative sentence caps the whole §7 sweep at 'that list', so an undetected empty derivation turns the entire test sweep into a no-op that closes green. (Distinct from the recorded finding that the sweep has an upper bound and no lower bound: that one is about the sweep's size, this one is about the designated observer being blind to the failure it is designated to catch.) A secondary reading tension sits in the same two paragraphs: the hazard is placed in the spec on the stated grounds that it 'belongs here rather than in acceptance', and its enforcement is then assigned to acceptance three lines later.

resolved.evidence: Measured rather than argued: with the derivation forced to return nothing, the check exits 1 in both arrangements -- 'derivation produced nothing, which is a broken derivation rather than a result' fires before any set comparison, and the stated count also disagrees. The set equality is never reached, so it cannot pass vacuously.

suggestion: State the emptiness guard explicitly rather than leaving it implied by set equality. One sentence in §7.1 suffices, e.g.: 'A zero-length list fails the check regardless of set equality, and the derivation command recorded in the file must include `--no-ext-diff`' — or hand the assertion to the acceptance directly ('the file is non-empty and its recorded derivation command contains `--no-ext-diff`'). If `scripts/check-measured-claims.py` already fails an empty list by way of the declared 'of the order of a hundred functions' claim, say so in the sentence that names the check, since today the reader has to assume it.

finding: The round-15/16 repair chain ends with §8.1 as the canonical home of the phase qualifier for CLAUDE.md's register-a-check rule, and the correction landed in every document it names. It does not name the instruction's second emitter, which is tp itself. Run on the current tree against this spec, `tp review spec/0.34.0.md --status` returns next_action = "register a check for the recurring \"measured-claim-not-reproducible\" class (tp set --workflow checks='[{\"class\":\"measured-claim-not-reproducible\",\"cmd\":\"…\"}]'), then run the next review round" -- the exact class §7.1 records as the registration that should not have been made in this phase, recommended again today with no phase condition. The branch (internal/engine/nextaction.go, precedence step 3) fires on class frequency alone and excludes only `over-specification`, so a phase qualifier cannot reach it; Non-Goal 1 fences that string out of this release, which makes naming it, not fixing it, the available disposition. It is worth naming because §1 schedules this release before v0.35.0's unattended run on the grounds that "every defect above is one an unattended loop multiplies", and next_action is the field an unattended driver consumes as its single next step: the operator who reads CLAUDE.md gets the qualifier, a loop that reads next_action does not. Low, not medium: next_action is documented as advisory and read-only, CLAUDE.md is loaded every cycle in this repo, and the mechanize branch is unreachable once the review converges. Everything else in the record verified against the shipping text this round rather than the evidence line -- both halves of the round-16 correction landed (§7.1:193-195 and §8.1:258-262 now agree, and the script docstring opens with what it guards); no retracted phrase ("verifies nothing", "bought nothing", "only ever see ... PENDING", "seven rounds") survives anywhere in the tree; 16 mutations against a clone of HEAD reproduce every property rounds 7-14 built (correct 100-entry list + declaration deleted exits 0 with no PENDING, and a trailing `## Notes` section still passes, while 99 entries, a fabricated entry, 50 duplicates, entries beside the declaration, an empty list without the declaration, a missing heading, 10 entries under a following `###` or `#` heading, a moved or reworded window, a dropped --no-ext-diff, a reworded match rule and a stale count all exit 1); the single `wontfix` still holds (deleting the declaration alone exits 1); and every re-derivable claim reproduces -- 1099 test functions in the tree ("of the order of a thousand"), 100 across 16 files for v0.32.0..v0.33.0, -race at 18.47-19.49s against 14.95-16.09s (1.15x-1.30x, inside "between a tenth and a half again"), `tp bogus` exit 1 vs `tp audit --bogus-flag` exit 2, all six §8.3 flags registered and absent from every document, the §11.6 quote present in spec/0.23.0.md §8, spec/0.34.0-candidates.md present, suppression carried in the r7-r14 prompts (eight rounds) and gone from r15 on, and exactly three `measured-claim-not-reproducible` findings in round 15.

resolved.evidence: Accepted with the reason recorded and a forward home: Non-Goal 1 fences tp's own next_action emitter out of this release. Carried to spec/0.35.0-candidates.md, where it matters because the unattended driver is that field's consumer.

suggestion: One clause where the rule now lives, or nothing. Either §8.1 names tp's own next_action register-a-check directive as the same instruction's second emitter, records that changing it is out of scope under Non-Goal 1, and carries it to spec/0.34.0-candidates.md the way Non-Goal 2 carries `scope`/`audit_converge_on`; or §8.1 states plainly that the qualifier is operator-side and that tp's advisory suggestion is deliberately left unqualified. Do not add a task for it: this is a record-keeping clause in a release governed by subtraction, and an accepted low with the reason recorded is a legitimate close.
